answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake at the gate, not on account names. Each miner must lock collateral before answering, and the ledger burns part of it when a challenge is graded sloppy or machine-copied. Cheap alt-accounts stop being cheap: the attacker pays the lock plus that burn on every clone, so a farm's cost scales with its headcount. A thousand bots bleed a thousand fees before one reward lands. That tradeoff sets the horizon we tune for, pushing the nadir of profitable fraud far above what a bare keypair allows. Dense as jade, hard to fake.
